result.summary: This PR fixes a bug where disabling network activity (via -networkactive=0 or setnetworkactive false) causes the node's saved block-relay-only anchor peers to be lost, since anchors.dat gets overwritten with an empty list on shutdown. It introduces a mutex-guarded m_anchors that is populated from current block-relay-only connections when the network is deactivated, consumed only while the network is active, and used as a fallback source when dumping anchors.dat at shutdown if there are no live connections. The PR went through several approach revisions after extensive review, including fixing a data race around fNetworkActive and correcting an anchor-count/ordering bug found by reviewers.
result.problem: Users who disable network activity and then cleanly shut down lose their previously-saved anchor peers, weakening the node's eclipse-attack defense on the next restart. This affects anyone using -networkactive=0 or the setnetworkactive RPC, as reported first-hand by the author and reproduced by danielabrozzoni.

open_concerns: Whether anchors should also be reloaded/refreshed when network is disconnected due to loss of internet (not just explicit networkactive=0) remains an open question, deferred as a follow-up by consensus.
Whether to restore anchors automatically when network is later re-enabled via setnetworkactive true was raised by luke-jr; author deferred to a follow-up.
resolved_concerns: Data race between setting fNetworkActive and capturing current connections, found by danielabrozzoni, fixed by capturing anchors before flipping the flag.
Anchor ordering/count mismatch when saving more than MAX_BLOCK_RELAY_ONLY_ANCHORS peers, found by w0xlt, fixed with a resize.
ThreadOpenConnections still consuming/popping anchors while network inactive, found by willcl-ark, fixed by skipping the anchor branch entirely when inactive.
Test structure and commit ordering nits from danielabrozzoni, addressed by reordering commits and consolidating tests.

result.card: This PR fixes a real bug where disabling network activity (via -networkactive=0 or setnetworkactive) causes bitcoind to overwrite anchors.dat with an empty list on shutdown, silently discarding the node's saved eclipse-attack-resistant peer anchors. It adds a mutex-guarded m_anchors store populated from live block-relay-only connections at deactivation time, and used as a fallback when dumping anchors at shutdown. Review was extensive over many months: danielabrozzoni gave a detailed security analysis calling it low-risk but worthwhile, and multiple reviewers (willcl-ark, w0xlt) found and got fixed a data race and an anchor-ordering bug in later revisions. The PR is now approved by willcl-ark with no open objections, though it has an open conflict with willcl-ark's own related PR #34486. Priority is moderate: it protects a real but narrow security property (eclipse resistance on restart) rather than fixing an actively exploited hole.
